newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end higher, confidence rising.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end higher, confidence rising.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished mostly higher Wednesday after a session in which the market showed growing confidence of more price gains.

"I think the market mood has improved a lot over the past few days," said a trader, pointing to the fact that most players are now beginning to believe the Federal Reserve will only hike rates by 25 basis points in May.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was flat at 91-3/4, the Par Brady was up 1/4 64-1/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 rose $0.13 to 126.18.
Another trader said the market had now more or less discounted a 25-basis-point U.S. rate hike and that the expectation was that such a hike would be the last one this year.
However, the Argentine market was slightly cautious as it will be shut for Labor Day Thursday ahead of the key U.S. labor report on Friday. U.S. markets are open Thursday.
The second trader said even if the market fell from its highs during this session, the market was kept afloat by key support levels.
Call money rates rose to 5.48 percent from 5.28 percent.
